extraction_note: Filing reports Aerospace & Defense as a single blended end-use market bucket. No specific Pentagon Program Elements (PE numbers), no named DoD programs of record, no named DoD customers, no IDIQ/program-of-record narratives. Defense exposure is Tier-3 / sub-tier specialty alloy supplier; the only named tier-1 customer is Howmet Aerospace (formerly Arconic) which was a 10% customer in FY20 but fell below 10% in FY21/FY22. The J-Book divergence pattern (named PE -> unfunded) has near-zero surface area in this filing.

claims.claim_text: Aerospace and Defense end-use market generated $790.2 million in FY2022 net sales, representing 43% of total net sales, up from $710.9M (48% mix) in FY2021 and down from $1,313.7M (60% mix) in FY2020.
claims.subject: Carpenter Technology
claims.object_value: $790.2M FY22 / 43% of net sales (recovering from COVID trough)
claims.notes: Aggregated A&D bucket; NOT decomposed into commercial-aero vs DoD. From context (jet engines, Howmet customer), majority is commercial aerospace, not DoD direct.

queries.rationale: Test whether J-Book corpus indexes Carpenter as a primary contractor on any specific PE
Confirm whether Carpenter has any direct DoD prime obligations (vs. sub-tier supplier through Howmet/GE/PW)

claims.claim_text: Forward-looking growth expectation: 'we expect to see continued growth across our end-use markets, especially in Aerospace, Defense and Medical applications, where customers are still ramping to pre-pandemic levels.'
claims.subject: Carpenter Technology
claims.object_value: FY23+ growth in Aerospace, Defense, Medical driven by post-COVID ramp
claims.source_quote: Looking ahead, we expect to see continued growth across our end-use markets, especially in Aerospace, Defense and Medical applications, where customers are still ramping to pre-pandemic levels.
claims.notes: Generic recovery narrative; no specific program named. Forward expectation is tied to commercial aero ramp + medical, not a named DoD program-of-record. Materiality of DoD-specific portion is low.

claims.claim_text: Backlog grew nearly 3x year-over-year to $1,539.3 million as of June 30, 2022 (from $529.3M at June 30, 2021), 'the majority of which is expected to be shipped within fiscal year 2023'.
claims.subject: Carpenter Technology
claims.object_value: $1,539.3M backlog, ~$1,010M YoY increase, most shippable in FY23
claims.source_quote: As of June 30, 2022, we had a sales backlog of orders excluding surcharge, believed to be firm, of approximately $1,539.3 million, the majority of which is expected to be shipped within fiscal year 2023.
claims.notes: Backlog is aggregate across all end-use markets; not allocated to DoD-specific programs. Treated as control claim — not a J-Book-grounded assertion.

claims.claim_text: Howmet Aerospace Inc. (formerly Arconic Inc.) accounted for ~10% of net sales in FY2020 (90% via SAO, 10% via PEP); no single customer reached the 10% threshold in FY2021 or FY2022.
claims.subject: Carpenter Technology
claims.object_value: Howmet ~10% in FY20; below threshold in FY21/FY22
claims.source_quote: One customer, Howmet Aerospace Inc. (formerly Arconic Inc.), accounted for approximately 10 percent of net sales for the year ended June 30, 2020. ... No single customer accounted for 10 percent or more of total net sales for the years ended June 30, 2022 and June 30, 2021.
claims.notes: Howmet is the only named customer. Howmet is a tier-1 engine-structures supplier (CFM/GEnx/V2500/LEAP/GE9X); routes Carpenter's alloy into commercial AND defense engine platforms but Carpenter does not name the downstream platform.

queries.rationale: Look for Howmet's mention of Carpenter as a supplier (counterparty corroboration)

claims.claim_text: Carpenter is a 'recognized leader in high-performance specialty alloy-based materials and process solutions for critical applications in the aerospace, defense, medical, transportation, energy, industrial and consumer end-use markets', with competitors numbering 'less than ten' in high-value demanding applications.
claims.subject: Carpenter Technology
claims.object_value: Leader in specialty alloys; <10 competitors in high-value demanding apps
claims.source_quote: There are less than ten companies producing one or more similar products that we consider our major competitors for our high-value products used in demanding applications, particularly in our Aerospace and Defense and Energy end-use markets.
claims.notes: Market-structure claim; not a specific program claim. Control claim.
